content.title: About
content.content: Lean pork steak is a cut taken from the low‑fat parts of the pig, such as the tenderloin or loin. It contains minimal intramuscular fat, is high in protein, and is often used in diet‑focused meals. When cooked properly it stays juicy and tender.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lean pork provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g.
Compared with beef, pork cooks faster and needs less time on the grill.
In traditional Russian cuisine, lean pork cuts were used for kotleti and baked dishes.
Pork is a good source of B‑vitamins, especially thiamine (B1), which supports the nervous system.
When stored correctly in the fridge, a lean steak stays fresh for 3‑4 days.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Protein is essential for muscle growth, repair, and immune function.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Lean pork fits well into calorie‑controlled and low‑saturated‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Thiamine, niacin and B6 aid metabolism and support nervous system health.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Pork supplies zinc, iron and phosphorus, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Creatine content
items.content: Creatine improves muscular energy metabolism, beneficial for intense training.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Raw or undercooked pork may contain Salmonella or Trichinella; cook to an internal temperature of 63 °C.

items.title: Sodium in processed cuts
items.content: If the steak is pre‑marinated it can be high in sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may have a food allergy to pork proteins.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout should limit intake of lean pork.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Lean pork steak is best grilled, pan‑seared, or baked. Slice thinly for salads, add to vegetable stews, or use in sandwiches. Finish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a light soy glaze for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the steak in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a vacuum‑sealed bag at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
